final:
All 53 requested tests pass, including the new regression test.

**What I found.** The attachment API in `src/backend/InvenTree/common/api.py` derives permissions from the model an attachment belongs to. Create, update, delete, and bulk delete all check the user's rights against that target model. Read requests did not. Any authenticated user, even one with no roles at all, could list every attachment in the system and fetch any attachment by ID. That exposed file download URLs, filenames, and comments for parts, purchase and sales orders, companies, build orders, and stock items the user was never allowed to view.

**What I changed.** I added a `filter_queryset` override to the shared attachment view mixin. For read requests it restricts the queryset to model types where the user holds view permission, using the same two checks the write paths already use. Hidden attachments return 404 on the detail endpoint and are omitted from the list. Write requests are left unfiltered so the existing explicit permission checks still return their descriptive 403 responses, which an existing test depends on.

**Test added.** A new test in `common/test_api.py` confirms a role-less user sees nothing, an unrelated role still sees nothing, and granting view on the target model exposes the attachment.

Test result:

```

OK
```

CHOICE: Filtered attachment list and detail reads by the user's view permission on the target model type, because every write path already enforced model-based permissions while reads leaked all attachment metadata and file URLs to any authenticated user.
